title: SCIM: idle-session drain + quarantine policy for staged deprovisioning
creator: Ava Collins
description:
Problem: Customers report accidental user removals when upstream IdP sends delete events during bulk provisioning windows. Current SCIM flow performs immediate deletion (or fast suspend) which can break ongoing sessions, background tasks, and audit correlation. We need a safer staged-deprovision flow that: 1) drains active sessions gracefully, 2) quarantines users for a configurable TTL before irreversible deletion, and 3) provides deterministic retry/backoff for idempotent SCIM operations with visibility for operators.

Scope: Implement an 'idle-session drain' step and a 'quarantine TTL' state in the provisioning state machine. This ticket covers the state transitions, audit logging augmentation, and retry/backoff policy integration for user and group deletes. It does NOT include UI changes to Console; Console follow-up ticket will surface quarantine lists and manual restore controls.

Goals: 
- Prevent data loss from premature deletions during transient IdP flapping.
- Preserve SLOs for deprovisioning pipelines (bounded by configurable TTL).
- Make operations observable: per-tenant metrics for quarantined-count, drain-duration, retry-failures, and manual restores.

Contraints/Non-goals: 
- No change to SCIM schema. We remain API-compatible with existing IdPs; we distinguish behavior by configuration flag per-tenant (default ON for enterprise tiers).

Design summary: 
- New user lifecycle states: ACTIVE -> DRAINING -> QUARANTINED -> FINAL_DELETED.
- On delete event: if tenant flag is set, mark user as DRAINING and send SCIM 200 to IdP; asynchronously start drain job that waits for active sessions to become idle or max-drain-time. After drain completes, move to QUARANTINED with quarantine_ttl default 72h. During QUARANTINED, deprovisioning can be reversed via a 'restore' operation (SCIM PATCH or admin API). After TTL expiry, transition to FINAL_DELETED and perform irreversible cleanup.

Observability and audit: Every state transition must emit audit entries with actor (IdP or operator), correlation_id, and reason. Emit Prometheus metrics and an SLI dashboard: quarantined_users_total, drain_success_ratio, drain_latency_seconds_bucket, quarantine_restores_total, final_delete_failures_total.

Retry semantics: SCIM deletes are idempotent; implement exponential backoff with jitter and a capped retry budget for background finalize jobs. For failures that are transient (network, 5xx infra), schedule retries; for permanent 4xx policy errors, mark as FAILED and send operator alert.

Security considerations: Quarantine must not allow access to customer resources. While in QUARANTINED, all tokens should be invalidated. We must ensure audit logs correlate tokens to pre-deletion activity for forensic needs.
acceptance_criteria: Can configure per-tenant staged-deprovisioning flag via admin API
Delete SCIM event returns 200 immediately while user transitions to DRAINING
Drain job respects max-drain-time and terminates gracefully
Quarantine TTL default 72h configurable; manual restore API restores to ACTIVE and logs audit entry
After TTL expiry, FINAL_DELETED performed and irreversible cleanup executed
Metrics and audit events emitted for each transition and available in Console/monitoring
Retry/backoff implemented with capped retry budget; operator alerts for permanent failures
implementation_notes:
Technical path: add state column to provisioning table (string). Add orchestrator job 'deprovisioner' that consumes delete intents from a queue and runs drain->quarantine->finalize flow. Reuse existing KV cache invalidation API for token revocation. Prefer database-friendly transitions (compare-and-swap) to avoid races across multiple reconciler workers. Use existing rate-limiter for finalize phase to avoid thundering herd on downstream cleanup.

Trade-offs considered: immediate delete reduces surface area of stale accounts and simplifies billing reconciliation, but increases risk of accidental data loss. Quarantine increases storage/retention but provides safe rollback. We scoped quarantine to tenant-level opt-in for enterprise to reduce default storage/complexity for self-serve customers.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flag gated implementation deployed to staging. 2) Smoke tests with synthetic IdP events and drain scenarios. 3) Canary rollout to 5% of production tenants with flag ON (monitor drain latency and quarantined counts). 4) If stable, enable for enterprise tenants by default; provide opt-out for customers. 5) Post-rollout: run a 2-week monitor period and collect metrics for SLOs.

Rollback: disable flag and re-run reconciler to fast-track DRAINING->FINAL_DELETED if a fix is needed. Maintain a live runbook for manual restores and emergency cleanup.
qa_steps: Unit tests for state transitions and compare-and-swap semantics
Integration tests simulating concurrent delete + restore events
End-to-end test with staging IdP that issues delete events during active session — assert tokens invalidated and drain respects max-drain-time
Chaos test: network partitions during finalize to validate retry budget and dead-letter behaviour
Load test: simulate bulk deletes on a tenant and verify rate-limits and downstream throttling prevent spikes
